answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with earned, decaying weight: an identity gains influence only after thirty days of verified useful work — completed jobs and peer-confirmed deliveries — and that weight shrinks by a fixed delta each idle week, so a dormant haven of bought accounts loses power. Each unit of weight is tied to one marble of history, a tamper-evident record of one job. Forging a thousand such histories means a thousand months of real work; buying accounts buys only empty history, and faking a month of verified output per identity costs far more than one extra vote is worth.
